class_guess: multi-level binary counter: #11-style carry M over fueled units, walls migrate unit to unit, edge fossils = Pascal rows
summary: Fueled-unit binary counter, rules closed (27,813/27,813 to 1e9); halting = a k=1 unit losing the fuel race.
mechanism: Wall view: 1-blocks of length 3g+2 (11, 1^5, ...) are unit boundaries with g glued walls; 3j+1 (1111, 1^7, ...) are passive stacks; units are `x M m Q .. y` (lead M = 00/1111 is the bit, y = fuel); the leftmost block is the edge. Carry M: leads 1111->00 up to the first 00->1111, every touch burns fuel.

Markers flow right: a passive wall that reaches the boundary glues, then becomes the next unit's lead (unglue S) while that unit's old lead turns passive. The edge grows by 3 per overflow and fossilizes into passive stacks that seed the Pascal rows; resets turn the tail into a new LSB unit.

Halts iff F reads a 1 after `00`: only a single-marker unit running dry does that. Its margin y-(2T-bit) is constant between resets; non-halting needs the reset ratio a_{n+1}/a_n < 2 (observed 1.79-1.86). No halt to 1e11 (direct) or in 3M more macro increments.

template.note: Level 0 is #11's per-carry M (one macro step per carry, every touch burns fuel). There is no global re-pairing O: new LSB units enter at the right, old units fossilize at the left into an unbounded Pascal-triangle zone (depth ~ log t). #3's down-counter with ghost-phase J does not fit (this counter increments).

strategy: Stage 3: an invariant for the k=1 fuel race (margin y-(2T-bit) >= 0 for every episode), closed under all rules and tested on the macro simulator. Needs a bound on the reset ratio a_{n+1}/a_n < 2, set by the Pascal-structured arrival schedule from U_0/U_1.
risks: The invariant must control future fuel-race episodes, whose start depends on the arrival schedule from an unbounded Pascal-structured fossil zone: far beyond #11's INV.
The reset ratio a_{n+1}/a_n oscillates slowly (1.79-1.86 observed) with no closed form; a proof needs a uniform bound below 2.
Rules are validated, not proved: the macro step uses shift rules over alternating stretches that a Coq proof would have to establish one by one.
